processing: Little is published about the method; as with Chinese black teas generally, the leaf is withered, rolled, oxidised and dried.
harvest_season: Spring is the main picking season in Zayü's tea gardens; other details are not well documented.
appearance_dry: Typical of Chinese black teas of its kind: dark, twisted strips.
taste_profile: Few tasting accounts exist, so its character is an open question; a smooth, sweet cup is what its class would suggest.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for Chinese black tea; adjust by taste.

vintage_note: A young, small-volume regional tea, normally sold from the current year's harvest as is usual for Chinese black tea. Ask for the harvest year and drink it within a year or two.
description:
Chayu Black Tea comes from Zayü County in Nyingchi, in the far south-east of Tibet, next to India's Assam. Few people think of Tibet as a tea-growing place, which is what makes this tea a curiosity.

Zayü makes white, green and black tea from the same small industry, and how the black is processed isn't well recorded. The general method of withering, rolling, oxidising and drying is the safe assumption.

There are few tasting notes to go on, so approach it with curiosity and a gentle first steep. Expect variation, since this is a small region.

It is rare outside China. If you find some, ask for the harvest year.
history:
Little is documented in the sources checked about when tea, or black tea, began in Zayü.

In 2024 Zayü's white, black and green teas were added to the national agriculture ministry's list of notable regional products. Today the county has about 21,000 mu of tea gardens.
